title: Geo-driven retention SKU and EU/UK SCCs playbook with escrow archive option
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable playbook and experiment plan to test geo-driven retention SKUs (EU, UK, US, APAC) tied to explicit escrow/archive options and updated SCCs language for enterprise contracts. Scope covers pricing packaging experiments, contract addendum templates, internal legal questionnaire responses, and a self-serve flag surface for retention/region selection in the console. We will define measurable hypotheses (conversion and ACV uplift), draft contract language for SCC adoption and subprocessor transparency, and implement telemetry to evaluate negotiation time and legal review friction.

Scope (in): pricing SKUs, contract addendum templates, SCCs assessment recommendations, subprocessor disclosure checklist, console flag UX, telemetry & dashboards.
Scope (out): changes to core data storage implementation or multi-region replication architecture (engineering tickets created separately).

Acceptance criteria:
- Draft contract addendum with EU/UK SCCs phrasing approved by Legal and Security (sign-off captured in Confluence).
- Pricing SKUs defined for 3 retention tiers with mapped list prices and discount levers for committed Dedicated seats.
- Self-serve console flag prototype for retention+region selection with product and design acceptance tests.
- Telemetry dashboard showing conversion from quote to signed contract, average negotiation days, and expected MRR impact.
- Experiment plan with sample size, cohorts, and KPI targets (conversion delta >=2.0% or ACV uplift >=8%).
acceptance_criteria: Legal and security sign-off on contract addendum text
Pricing SKU table for 3 retention tiers with clear tradeoffs
Console flag prototype with product/UX review
Telemetry dashboard tracking negotiation days and conversion
Runbook for sales on answering SCCs/subprocessor questions
comments: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: PM + Legal + Security + Sales Ops. Agreed high-level tiers: 30d standard, 90d sealed archive, 180d escrow+archive. Sales will pilot UK/EU deals first.
2025-02-18 - Legal feedback: prefer SCCs mapping doc and require explicit subprocessor disclosure in addendum. Security requests encryption-at-rest clause for escrow buckets.
2025-02-24 - Design: initial console flag flows created (link in artifacts). UX decision: retention selection should appear during plan configuration stage, not checkout modal.
2025-02-28 - Engineering sync: ENG to expose retention selection as token in billing API. ENG asks for telemetry events: retention_choice, contract_signed_region, negotiation_duration_days.
2025-03-03 - Draft addendum uploaded to drive; shared with Legal for redline (PR linked). Sales ops requested a one-page cheat sheet for SDRs on answering SCC questions.
2025-03-05 - Decision: run A/B experiment (self-serve SKU vs. sales-assisted negotiated SKU) for 6 weeks with EU/UK targeted cohorts. Next: finalize pricing table and schedule legal sign-off meeting.
2025-03-05 - Blocker noted: need Security approval on escrow storage location and KMS integration before customer-facing language is finalized.

tradeoffs: Higher retention/escrow SKUs increase revenue but add legal negotiation overhead and longer sales cycles
Self-serve SKUs reduce negotiation time but may not capture maximum ACV for large enterprise buyers
Aggressive SCC language may require engineering changes to prove data locality/compliance which delays launch
notes: We should track legal review time as a leading indicator of friction; add 'legal_review_days' to telemetry.
Consider offering a short-term promotional discount for first 6 EU customers who sign up for escrow+archive to accelerate data for the experiment.
If Security cannot sign-off on escrow KMS pattern, fallback is to offer 'managed-archive' with additional contractual assurances rather than technical escrow.
